title: Two rooks
line: The ladder: rooks taking turns on the ranks.

steps.text: Two rooks mate without help from the king. One holds a row, the other checks on the next row, and they take turns, like a ladder.
The rook on a4 holds its row. Check the king with the other rook on the king's own row.
steps.hint: The rook on b1 moves straight up the board.
steps.after: The king cannot step down past either rook, so it must climb a row.

steps.text: Now the other rook takes its turn: check on the king's row.
steps.hint: The rook that held the row below goes up past its partner.

steps.text: Keep climbing. Check with the rook on b5.
steps.hint: Up the board, one row past your other rook.
steps.after: The king is on the edge.

steps.text: One more rung, and it is mate.
steps.hint: The rook on the row below checks along the back row.
steps.after: Checkmate. One rook holds the row in front of the king, the other checks on the edge.

steps.text: Here the black king stands near your rooks. A check from the rook on b3 would put it next to the king, and the king would take it.
Move that rook far along its row first, to the side away from the king.
steps.hint: Slide the rook toward the other rook's side of the board.
steps.after: The rook is far from the king, and your other rook still holds its row.

also.b3e3: That works too: the rook is far from the king. This lesson goes on with the rook on g3.

steps.text: Now the ladder goes on. Check on the king's row.
steps.hint: The rook on g3 moves up one row.
steps.after: The king must climb again. Take turns with the rooks until it reaches the edge.

summary: Two rooks take turns checking, one row higher each time. Keep them far from the king.
